title: the success-axis k x backoff-target selection surface re-drawn on three seeds and widened to k=6400 — post-hoc transforms of stored predictions, no training
purpose: the shipped cell (candidates J and K) was chosen on a SINGLE-SEED surface (exp_023).  exp_024 promoted that one cell to three seeds but never re-drew the surface.  This re-draws it.
changed_vs_exp_023_and_exp_026: the surface is drawn on THREE seeds (42/7/2024) with a SEPARATE argmin per seed; exp_023's surface was seed 42 alone
the k grid goes 7 -> 10 values: 1600, 3200 and 6400 are added
the high-k extension covers BOTH backoff targets; exp_026 extended `league` only, so k in {1600,3200,6400} x self and 6400 x league are measured here for the first time
an explicit enclosure test (is the argmin interior to the grid) on every surface, per seed and on the mean
an explicit self-vs-league crossing test along k
the block-vs-fold_2024 argmin gap is computed for BOTH targets (exp_026 had it for league only)
the seed-42 surface is gated cell-by-cell against exp_023's recorded 14 cells (GATE 5) — a check exp_023 could not run
run with OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 because exp_027 is training on the same box (pure numpy vector work; GATE 5 shows it changes nothing)
unchanged_vs_exp_023_and_exp_026: base vectors and their sha256, exp_004 F-mask, clip 1e-6, supply blocks 2022+2023, closed-form no-intercept slope, expanded d form, league term regrouped as L*k/(n+k), dev_k.py / backoff.py / offset.py / features_platoon.py / labels.py / exp016_ref.py / devgen.py byte-identical (sha asserted)

reproduction_gate.source: exp_024/metrics.json per_seed[seed].B_candidate.brier and .A_control.brier — READ from the record, not transcribed
reproduction_gate.on_fail: abort — the reused vectors or the inherited code are not exp_024's and nothing downstream is readable

gate5_exp023_surface_reproduction.what: exp_023's recorded 14 cells (7 k x 2 targets), seed 42, on the BLOCK surface and on fold_2024.  This is the strongest gate available: it checks every beta and every Brier, not one arm

label_isolation_check.note: no model is fitted here, so the design matrix is exp_024's; check (b) below is the operative one for this experiment

asof_independent_recheck.method: row_id -> season re-read from train.csv in a SECOND pass; the max season of the CONTRIBUTING ROW IDS is looked up in that independent map, not in the frame the tables were built from

surfaces.note: block = Brier on the pooled supply blocks 2022+2023 at the block-fitted beta (exp_023's registered SELECTION surface).  crossblock = fit one block, score the other, pooled.  fold_2024 is DIAGNOSTIC and selects nothing.

Q1_seed_stability_of_the_argmin.ask: does the three-seed block surface still point at S400_league (what candidates J and K ship)?
Q1_seed_stability_of_the_argmin.seed_sensitivity_verdict: the block surface picks the same cell on all three seeds

Q2_self_vs_league_and_crossing.ask: what does `self` do at high k, and does it cross `league`?

block_mean.convention: diff = self - league in Brier; diff < 0 means SELF wins

fold_2024_mean_DIAGNOSTIC.convention: diff = self - league in Brier; diff < 0 means SELF wins

42.convention: diff = self - league in Brier; diff < 0 means SELF wins

7.convention: diff = self - league in Brier; diff < 0 means SELF wins

2024.convention: diff = self - league in Brier; diff < 0 means SELF wins

Q2_self_vs_league_and_crossing.context: exp_028 measured the REVERSE axis and found `self` beating `league` at EVERY k it tried (k <= 3200).  On the success axis exp_026 found the opposite for k <= 800.  A crossing inside this grid would mean the preference is k-dependent, not axis-dependent.

Q3_block_vs_fold2024_argmin_gap.ask: does the block-surface argmin disagree with the fold_2024 argmin on `self` too, or only on `league`?
Q3_block_vs_fold2024_argmin_gap.discipline: fold_2024 is read AFTER every beta and every choice is fixed.  It prices the discipline; it never picks.

Q4_enclosure.ask: is the surface enclosed on both sides — is the minimum interior to the k grid?
Q4_enclosure.why: a minimum at the edge means the grid is too narrow and every conclusion about that region is provisional

selection.rule: argmin of the pooled-block Brier over all 20 cells, beta fitted on the same blocks.  fold_2024 is read only afterwards.
selection.NO_NEW_DEPLOYMENT: this experiment produces no candidate.  If the surface had pointed elsewhere that would be a finding to report, and any swap would go through its own three-seed promotion, leak audit and packager run.

conversion.sensitivity: brier 1e-6 = score 0.4003.  Every Brier here is full precision, so the converted numbers carry no rounding band of their own
conversion.caveat: local measurement is at iter 650 (<=2023 training); the deployed build is iter 7700 (<=2024).

leak_boundary.tables: a season-s row reads tables built on seasons <= s-1 only; asserted at runtime inside backoff.py / dev_k.py and again here by an independent second read of train.csv
leak_boundary.recovered_labels: the success numerator is a RECOVERED label of row t+1.  It is used only as the numerator of a frozen as-of table, never as a row-level input; group-constancy of all 30 checked vectors inside (season, pitcher, batter_hand, pitcher_hand) is asserted, which a row-level leak would break
leak_boundary.coef_fit: supply blocks 2022+2023 of the same seed, on that cell's own column; no beta ever sees 2024
leak_boundary.cell_choice: the grid is fixed by config.yaml before any 2024 number is read, and the cell is chosen on the block surface; fold_2024 is diagnostic only
leak_boundary.design_matrix: unchanged — no deviation is ever a model feature, and no training happens in this experiment
leak_boundary.missing: no sentinel fill anywhere; L=0 and d=0 mean 'apply no correction', the behaviour without the module
